summary.headline: 99215 billed at about 6x the rate expected for this panel, including on patients with no chronic conditions
summary.rationale: This provider billed 817 of 2,500 visits (32.7%) as 99215, against about 5.2% expected for their patients' complexity. The excess is present at every complexity level, not just among sick patients: 18.0% of visits on patients with 0 chronic conditions were 99215 (all-provider rate 2.1%), and 25.4% for patients with 1 condition (3.4%). The cited low-complexity 99215 visits carry minor diagnoses (rash R21, back pain M54.50, an annual follow-up Z09) on patients with no recorded chronic conditions, which would not ordinarily support the highest level. The high-complexity sample is defensible on its face (an 80-year-old with 7 conditions) but all three examples shown come from one patient, so it does not offset the pattern. No clinical documentation is available here, so this is a statistical pattern, not a finding.
next_steps: Request visit documentation (time spent, issues addressed) for the cited low-complexity 99215 claims
Check how many 99215 visits are for acute minor complaints (rash, URI, back pain) on patients with no chronic conditions
Look at the repeat patient in the high-complexity sample (P0215-N0682) to see whether their visit frequency is itself unusual

summary.headline: High 99215 share, but most of the gap tracks an unusually sick panel; a smaller residual remains at the top complexity band
summary.rationale: This provider billed 860 of 2,500 visits (34.4%) as 99215 against about 16.7% expected given patient complexity, so the screen flags them on both measures. But two thirds of their visits (1,669) are on patients with 5 or more chronic conditions, a much sicker panel than the all-provider mix, and at low complexity their rates look ordinary (3 conditions: 9.1% vs 8.7% for all providers; 0 to 2 conditions: 11 of 197 visits, too few to judge). The unexplained part is within the sickest band: 45.4% of 5+ condition visits were 99215 versus 29.8% for all providers. The cited high-complexity visits involve patients aged 76 to 89 with 8 conditions, which supports high acuity, though some list only one or two diagnosis codes (for example C0007470 lists only I10 for a patient with 8 conditions), so the visit-level documentation should be checked.
next_steps: Request documentation for 99215 visits that list only one or two diagnosis codes on patients with 8 conditions (for example C0007470)
Ask why 67% of the panel has 5+ conditions (specialty referrals, a nursing-facility or complex-care panel) before treating the volume as unusual
Compare the 45.4% vs 29.8% gap in the 5+ band against peers with similarly sick panels

summary.headline: Roughly a quarter of visits on patients with no or one chronic condition were billed 99215, about 10x the all-provider rate
summary.rationale: This provider billed 96 of 343 visits (28.0%) as 99215 against about 2.1% expected for their patients' complexity. The panel is low-complexity: 263 of 343 visits (77%) are on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, yet 25.0% and 23.4% of those visits were 99215 (all-provider rates 2.1% and 3.4%). The cited claims are 99215 visits for acute or minor presentations on patients with no recorded chronic conditions (URI J06.9, UTI N39.0, back pain M54.50, rash R21), which would not usually support the highest level. The practice is small (343 claims, 132 patients) and there are almost no high-complexity visits (13 visits on patients with 3 or more conditions), so the high end cannot be assessed and the sample is thin. As always, this rests on claims data alone with no clinical documentation.
next_steps: Request documentation (time, medical decision-making) for the cited 99215 visits
